Both saved. Reflection complete.

What this question exposed (genuinely generalizable):

The data extraction was flawless — I summed UK Total Liabilities for June 2000/2001/2002 = 573,088M USD, exactly matching the gold's basis. The entire error was the FX rate: I applied 0.66, gold used 0.65. The mismatch ratio was exactly 66/65 = 1.01538, a dead giveaway that digits were right and only the rounded rate was wrong.

The real lesson: when a question explicitly says "use the rate rounded to its hundredths place," you must **pre-round the rate to 2 dp before applying it** — this overrides the usual "carry full precision, round once" default. The true USD→GBP rate on 6/30/2002 was 1/1.5275 = 0.6547, which rounds half-up to 0.65, not 0.66.

Saved to:
- references/currency-and-geomean.md — full worked failure + the pre-round rule, the direction check (GBP-per-USD <1), and the "clean small-int ratio = rate error" diagnostic. (Reference already pointed-to from SKILL.md.)
- memory — compact cross-session pointer (had to compact two existing entries to fit; memory was at 99%).

This is a new, sharp pattern distinct from the prior currency note (which assumed multiply-by-2.79 USD/GBP and carry-full-precision). Worth saving.
